audit.why: Cassiopeia owns levels 1-5 outright on range and sustained damage, and the entry concedes them cleanly rather than pretending there is a trade pattern. From 6 it is Skill, which the 50.63 win rate supports. The packet levelChart disagrees only at Levels 4-5 and Level 6; the content chart's version is the better read, because Petrifying Gaze arriving at 6 is a spike for her, not for Sejuani, and the entry's own whys[4] says so.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 is described as the moment 'the math shifts' toward Sejuani, but whys[4] and spikes[1].text both say Cassiopeia wins the level 6 spike. The entry contradicts itself about who spikes at 6.
audit.why: Both readings are defensible and the difference is entirely whether Petrifying Gaze lands, which is exactly what makes it a Skill stage rather than a spike for either side. What was missing is the number that lets a player make that call: 825 range and 120 seconds at rank 1. A missed Petrifying Gaze is a two-minute window in which she has no answer to a Q-W-E chain, and the entry never tells the reader how long the reward for dodging lasts.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and mid now carry the 825 range and the facing rule; breakdown.cooldowns carries the 120s. The stage sides are unchanged.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Miasma grounding is present and correct — the one entry in this slice that already had its decisive interaction. But its cooldown is never given, Twin Fang's healing is never mentioned anywhere, and wants.foe[0] claims Cassiopeia stacks Grievous Wounds on you.
audit.why: Cassiopeia applies no Grievous Wounds. Nothing in her kit does, and a Sejuani reading that will assume her own healing is being cut and play a fight she should be winning differently. Twin Fang is the real omission on the other side: Riot's text is 'heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt', and it is a 0.75s cooldown ability she spams on a poisoned target — so a long fight against Cassiopeia without Grievous Wounds refills her while it drains you. The reader is told to buy nothing. And Miasma at 24/22/20/18/16 is the longest cooldown in the matchup: the entry correctly says it grounds Arctic Assault but never says that a spent Miasma is a 24-second window, which is the single most actionable number available here.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds removed from wants.foe[0]. Twin Fang's healing stated in whys[0], spikes[0].text and late, with Grievous Wounds named as the buy. Miasma's 24s is now in spikes[0].text, wants.you[0], mid and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0], whys[3], spikes[0].text and early say 'Permafrost armor'; late says the chain keeps her 'rooted'.
audit.why: Permafrost is a 1.5s targeted stun with no armour attached — the resistances are Frost Armor on Fury of the North, which returns only out of combat. That conditional is the whole reason Cassiopeia's poke works: it is not that she out-damages the armour, it is that she never lets Sejuani leave combat long enough to get it back. And nothing in Sejuani's kit roots: Permafrost stuns, and the Glacial Prison storm slows. A reader who believes they apply a root will misjudge what their team can follow up on.
audit.corrected: whys[0] now states the out-of-combat condition. late says 'holds her' rather than 'rooted'.

edits.after: Level 6 is where the math shifts — but only if you dodge Petrifying Gaze. It reaches 825 units and stuns only enemies facing her, so turn your back as it lands and you eat a slow instead. If it misses, Q into both Winter's Wrath arcs to fill the gauge, then Permafrost, is a full-power punish she cannot answer with no dash. Check Miasma before you commit: it grounds Arctic Assault outright, and at 24 seconds at rank 1 a spent Miasma is the longest safe window she gives you. Glacial Prison at this stage is a river weapon — landing it in a 2v1 is a near-certain kill.

edits.after: With Sunfire Aegis and a second tank item you are durable enough to absorb a full poison and Twin Fang cycle and still land the Permafrost stun, which flips the DPS equation — she needs sustained time on you that your CC denies. Buy Grievous Wounds: Twin Fang heals her for a share of every hit it lands, and a long fight without anti-heal refills her. In teamfights keep your back to her before engaging so Petrifying Gaze catches your backside and only slows, then launch Glacial Prison into the backline and Arctic Assault in behind it. She has no mobility to leave the blizzard, and the chain from Glacial Prison into Permafrost holds her long enough for your team to convert. She out-scales you in a pure 1v1; the structured fight is yours.

notes:
This was the strongest entry in the slice on arrival: Miasma's grounding of Arctic Assault is stated correctly in four fields, and the Petrifying Gaze facing rule is right. The gaps were numbers rather than mechanics.

FABRICATION REMOVED: wants.foe[0] said Cassiopeia stacks Grievous Wounds on you. No ability in her kit applies anti-heal.

The entry contradicts itself on the level 6 spike — mid says the math shifts to Sejuani, whys[4] and spikes[1].text say Cassiopeia wins it. I left both sides standing because the honest answer is that it depends on whether Petrifying Gaze lands, and added the numbers that let the reader judge. If the user wants one direction stated, that is a call about editorial voice rather than a fact I can settle.

The packet levelChart for this matchup gives Cassiopeia stages 0-2 and 4 and Sejuani 5-6, while content win[] gives Cassiopeia 0-3 and Skill for 4-6. They disagree at Levels 4-5 and Level 6. I did not flip any side; the content version is internally consistent with its own whys, the packet version is not.
